Date: 2026-08-03
Time: 14:00 - 14:42 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Orion Partnerships), Maya Gonzalez (Orion Solutions Architect), Ethan Li (Orion Head of Cloud Partnerships)

summary: Intro call between Redwood AE/SE and Orion Compute partnerships/solutions team. Orion exploring partnership to offer Redwood Dedicated and Private as a managed inference stack for their GPU/cloud customers and reseller channel. Main concerns: integration effort for billing & provisioning, network/VPC peering, KMS/encryption, and latency-cost tradeoffs for multi-tenant shared pools. Agreed next steps: share partner one-pager, run latency/cost calc, schedule technical deep-dive.
topics: Security and compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
Integration points: provisioning API, billing, SSO/SCIM
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we can do quick intros. I'm Sofia, AE at Redwood.
[00:06] Raj: Hey Sofia, Raj here, partnerships. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:09] Maya: Maya, solutions architect at Orion. Nice to meet you.
[00:12] Liam: Liam from Redwood infra, SE. I'll cover technical bits.
[00:16] Ethan: Ethan, I run cloud partnerships at Orion. Quick agenda?
[00:19] Sofia: Yeah, we'll cover who we are, what partnership models look like — hosted, dedicated, private — then dig into integration and security.
[00:27] Raj: Sounds good. Our high level: Orion sells GPU infra + managed services to ISVs and verticals. We're exploring bundling a best-in-class inference stack; Redwood came highly recommended.
[00:36] Maya: Key questions from our side: how much effort to integrate provisioning and billing, can we white-label, and what are latency profiles on hosted vs dedicated?
[00:45] Liam: Cool — on latency, short answer: hosted api is easiest but dedicated gives predictable throughput and better p99 latency. We do continuous batching and KV cache which helps for repeated prompts.
[00:56] Raj: When you say dedicated, is that reserved GPU pools managed by Redwood in our region, or do we host?
[01:02] Sofia: We have two flavors. Redwood Dedicated is reserved capacity in our infrastructure — you get isolated pools with commits. Redwood Private is a VPC or on-prem deployment where you operate control plane in your network and we ship the runtime or run a private control plane.
[01:16] Raj: Ok. For some enterprise customers we need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. Is that supported?
[01:22] Liam: Yes — Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and customer-managed keys, and we surface audit logs and RBAC. There are some network setup steps for peering and NAT, but it's standard.
[01:31] Maya: Any SOC2 or ISO attestation required from our side? Some of our customers will ask for SOC2 reports.
[01:36] Sofia: Redwood has SOC2 Type II and can provide compliance pack. For Private deployments the customer often runs additional audit controls; we also support fine-grained logging to integrate with SIEM.
[01:45] Ethan: From GTM — we're thinking two motions: 1) bundle Redwood Dedicated as a managed add-on in Orion marketplace, 2) deeper integration where Orion resells Private deployments to large customers. What's typical revenue split or partner margin?
[01:59] Sofia: We have partner programs with referral and reseller tracks; margins vary by commit volume. I'll share the partner one-pager and partner pricing ranges after the call.
[02:08] Raj: Perfect. On the technical side, can Redwood runtime run on A100s and on newer H100s? Some of our fleet is mixed.
[02:14] Liam: Yes — runtime supports multiple accelerator types; kernel selection and quantization profiles are tuned per architecture. For H100 we see better throughput on longer sequences; A100 still performs well. There may be different model variants/quantization tradeoffs.
[02:27] Maya: How do you handle model variants and rollouts? If we pin a customer to a particular model version, can we control rollouts?
[02:33] Sofia: Yes, all deployments support pinning and rollout policies; Console exposes canary and A/B rollouts and automatic fallback policies if a model fails.
[02:41] Raj: Latency/cost — for a 10k qps inference workload (small prompt/streaming) what ballpark numbers should we expect?
[02:49] Liam: We'll need more details — avg tokens per request, streaming vs batch, concurrency. But as a rough starting point, dedicated pools with batching lower per-token cost, hosted is simpler but can be ~20-40% higher unit cost depending on workload. We'll do a spreadsheet calculation.
[03:03] Ethan: Integration APIs — do you have provisioning APIs so Orion can programmatically create and decommission capacity for customers?
[03:09] Sofia: Yes, we have provisioning APIs and webhooks for lifecycle events; partner integrations commonly automate seat provisioning and billing.
[03:16] Maya: SSO? SCIM for user management?
[03:18] Liam: We support SAML/SSO and SCIM for enterprise accounts; for Private you can integrate with your IdP.
[03:24] Raj: A few customers will want on-prem air-gapped installs. Is that on the table?
[03:28] Sofia: We offer on-prem packages for regulated workloads; it's more of an enterprise engagement with professional services.
[03:34] Maya: Any hard dependencies on Kubernetes? Our stack uses a mix of k8s and bare metal tooling.
[03:38] Liam: Runtime can run in k8s but we also support VM-based deployments; the orchestration layer is flexible. We might need some adaptors for your provisioning system.
[03:47] Raj: Ok — security checklist: KMS, audit logs, SOC2, SSO, network peering. Anything else we should flag?
[03:54] Liam: Data retention and ability to opt-out of logging for sensitive workloads is available; we can configure retention windows. Also model outputs are not stored by default for hosted unless you opt in for debugging.
[04:05] Maya: Perf testing — can we run a joint benchmark in our region? We want latency numbers from a customer-facing edge.
[04:10] Sofia: Absolutely. Typical approach: Orion provides a sample workload and target SLAs, we run benchmarks against Dedicated in-region or Private in your environment. Liam will coordinate the benchmark plan.
[04:21] Ethan: On billing — we need clarity on how commits map to invoices and whether Orion can resell under our SKU.
[04:28] Sofia: We support reseller models; billing can be integrated via APIs or we can set up invoicing. I'd note pricing depends on commit size and support level.
[04:36] Raj: Competitors — some of our partners evaluate CoreWeave and Lambda Labs. How does Redwood differentiate?
[04:41] Liam: We focus on production-grade inference: predictable latencies, smart routing, caching, and a strong Console for observability. Also our partner program is aimed at enabling resell and co-sell.
[04:52] Maya: Do you support model hosting (customers bring their own models) and open model catalog?
[04:56] Sofia: Yes, BYOM is supported, and we maintain a curated model catalog and recommended quantization profiles.
[05:01] Raj: Questions from our security team — will you share SOC2 and details for audit?
[05:05] Sofia: Yes, we'll share the compliance pack; Liam can provide the technical controls list.
[05:10] Maya: Any known gotchas when integrating with our provisioning layer (we use a custom Terraform + API gateway)?
[05:15] Liam: Mostly mapping auth and service accounts; we'll likely build a connector that talks to your provisioning API. If you have terraform providers we can integrate.
[05:24] Raj: For GTM, do you have co-marketing/launch support for new channel partners?
[05:29] Sofia: Yes — co-marketing, joint webinars, and partner enablement materials are available in our partner portal.
[05:34] Ethan: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[05:36] Sofia: Recap: I'll send partner one-pager and partner pricing ranges; Liam will prepare latency/cost spreadsheet and proposed benchmark plan; Raj will share sample dataset and security contacts; schedule technical deep-dive week of 2026-08-17.
[05:50] Raj: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[05:52] Sofia: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites and materials.
[05:55] (call ends, small crosstalk)
